title: Bittensor Daily News — November 5, 2026
summary: Release 487 reaches Subtensor main with Gamma service credits and quantum-resistant wallet code, while the finalized chain still runs 486. SN58 Attune adds a robot-data platform and a proposed miner-reward route; SN38 ChronoLLM previews a 16B point-in-time model. Plus service listings, miner tooling, dated carry-forwards and verified chain archives.

ecosystem.headline: Release 487 reaches main; Gamma and wallet authorization still need activation
ecosystem.summary: Subtensor PR3294 merged to main at 02:47 UTC on November 5, or 9:47 PM Eastern November 4. The integrated release includes dollar-valued Gamma service credits, ML-DSA/Falcon wallets and key rotation, proxy/basket fixes, lock proxies and burn/recycle allocation slots with a combined 33% cap. Gamma is minted by burning subnet alpha; spending destroys credits, not a second batch of alpha. Credits are non-redeemable and cannot transfer between coldkeys. Gamma requires network-wide and subnet enablement; hashed/post-quantum authorization also defaults disabled. Today’s finalized collector still reports runtime 486 and GitHub’s latest release tag is v486. The merge provides code for integrators to review, not proof of a mainnet upgrade, enabled services, customer demand or executed burns.

updates.headline: SN9 IOTA announces open IOTA Decide 4B weights and distributed-training details
updates.summary: November 4 afternoon carry-forward, already published in that edition: Macrocosmos announced SN9 IOTA’s first public model on November 4 at 12:11 PM Eastern. The IOTA Decide 4B v0.4 repository exposes Apache-2.0 weights, a model card and a loader; its file history predates today’s announcement. The text-only model takes a state and a typed question and returns probabilities for the available answers, using one forward pass per question rather than generating a chat response. The team describes fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B across 16 independently hosted RTX A4000 GPUs using streaming DiLoCo. That training account was not independently reproduced. Builders can inspect and self-host the artifact, but v0.4 requires the bundled letter_decide.py loader: ordinary chat-generation serving changes its behavior. The card reports a 78.6 JevBench composite and says leaderboard listing is pending because the newer question draw has not yet been equated. Accordingly, this report does not endorse the announcement’s top-ten or Pareto-frontier ranking as an established like-for-like result.

updates.headline: SN15 ORO outlines a shift from shopping agents to business simulations
updates.summary: In its November 4 blog, ORO says it has built an initial set of business simulation environments and is shifting from personal-shopping agents toward AI operating commerce businesses. The planned SN15 task emphasizes long-horizon decisions, delayed consequences and coherent strategy; miners would improve agents against these environments. The team describes public launch as coming soon without an exact date. The announcement establishes a new research direction and claimed internal preparation, not a completed public launch, customer adoption or verified revenue.

sources.label: SN15 ORO November 4 strategy and planned simulation launch

updates.ratingReason: A concrete change in the planned research and miner task; public launch and business outcomes remain pending.

updates.headline: SN36 Weir adds manual-review handling for GPU eligibility
updates.summary: A November 5 commit adds review paths that can end a GPU’s probation early or account for disputed GPUs in idle-pay calculations. The documentation says disputed GPUs are not offered for rent, and failed checks display PENDING_REVIEW. This separates earning eligibility from sellable capacity in the code. No affected GPU decision, actual payout or customer rental was independently executed.

updates.headline: SN38 ChronoLLM previews a 16B point-in-time model; weights are still forthcoming
updates.summary: On November 4 at 9:07 AM Eastern, SN38 ChronoLLM said pre-training was almost done for a 16B mixture-of-experts model with a 16K-token context. Its published chart compares model vintages by training-data cutoff and reports gains over prior point-in-time models. These are the team’s measurements, not independently reproduced scores or proof that lookahead bias is eliminated. The practical goal is reasoning over historical information without later data leaking into the task. The original says the model will be released; Const Reborn’s amplification does not turn that preview into four completed releases.

updates.headline: SN41 Almanac updates its prediction-market client and order documentation

This review inspected code and documentation only and did not place an order or test a financial transaction.

updates.headline: SN46 Instant merges overlapping signer support for validator key rotation
updates.summary: Instant merged validator PR13 on November 5 at 17:18 UTC. PLATFORM_SIGNER can now contain a comma-separated list of approved SS58 keys, letting operators retain an old signer while introducing a new one. Summaries must be signed by a listed key, and verification logs identify which signer was used. This provides an overlap mechanism for key rotation; the merge does not establish that operators have deployed it or that an actual platform-key rotation occurred.

updates.headline: SN58 Attune links Horizon robot-data work to a 70% miner-emission route
updates.summary: On November 5, Attune’s 0.3.0 code added Horizon, Robotensor’s robot-data platform, alongside the Vector policy competition. The public site offers phone-controlled simulated robot tasks and first-person recordings through request-access flows. The repository describes 30% of miner emission for Vector and 70% for one Horizon vault, with weekly off-chain contributor payouts by points. That denominator is the miner bucket, not all subnet emission or an eTAO owner/validator split. The checked-in network vault map is empty; code says an unregistered or unset vault share burns. The public rewards page at review showed zero contributors/points and said rewards were being calculated but not yet sent. The platform and code are accessible; a live 70% vault payment, customer adoption and contributor payouts were not verified.

updates.headline: SN75 Hippius adds share-link comments and viewing insights
updates.summary: Hippius announced the sharing update on November 5 at 09:23 UTC. Its documentation describes comments, reactions and per-link viewing insights for shared captures. The privacy boundary matters: comments are encrypted with the link key, while reactions and view counts are not encrypted; ordinary link previews also expose the preview image and filename. Owners can toggle these features per link, and detailed recording analytics depend on the plan. This is a documented collaboration feature, not an independently audited security guarantee.

updates.ratingReason: A practical, documented collaboration update with clear privacy and plan limits; not a major ecosystem breakthrough.

updates.headline: SN80 OpenRoboto announces a commercial data pilot with Vulcan Shield Hungary
updates.summary: OpenRoboto’s November 5 X announcement follows a November 3 press release describing a commercial robotics-data pilot at a material-preparation workstation in Békéscsaba, Hungary. The planned sequence is to simulate the workstation, capture operators’ first-person demonstrations with OR-S1 headsets, then train and test task-specific robot models. The release includes a statement attributed to Vulcan Shield Hungary’s financial director and explicitly places the current work in simulation and data capture. Model validation, on-site robotic testing and deployment remain later stages. Vulcan Shield’s own website confirms its Hungarian manufacturing facility, but its reviewed press page did not separately announce this pilot. No contract value, received payment or production-robot performance was verified. The named industrial task provides a concrete setting for evaluating the subnet’s robotics data; Const’s November 5 amplification is commentary, not deployment evidence.

updates.headline: SN81 Reliquary releases open Teutonic-I-Reliquary 9B weights
updates.summary: Announced November 5 at 10:48 AM Eastern, Teutonic-I-Reliquary is a downloadable 9B reasoning and coding model under Apache-2.0. Its public repository contains four BF16 weight shards, a tokenizer, configuration and usage instructions; the files were uploaded November 4. The team attributes the base to SN3 Teutonic, trainer compute to SN51 Lium, agent sandboxes to SN4 Targon and data, rollouts and evaluations to SN81 Reliquary miners. It reports an October 22–November 2 asynchronous RL run of 158 steps and 15.7 billion trained tokens. Its model card reports 43.6% versus Qwen3.5-9B’s 35.1% on 486 SWE-bench Verified tasks using the same mini-swe harness and protocol; these are team evaluations, not an independently reproduced 500-task leaderboard result. The model leads on five of eight listed benchmarks and trails on GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and TMax. A public recorded-run dashboard supplies checkpoint history; declared GPU models are not hardware attestations. The release gives builders weights and an evaluation protocol to test, while the promised Gumbel-substitution technical report remains forthcoming.

updates.headline: SN108 ChipForge lets miners replace a queued design without losing its place
updates.summary: The November 4 Neuron 1.0.2 commit adds miner_cli.py replace, optionally identifying a submission. Documentation says the replacement keeps the original queue position and consumes no extra submission slot, draws new hidden tests and defaults to a limit of three replacements. Once evaluation starts, replacement is unavailable, with a documented 409 response. This gives miners a way to fix a design before a validator picks it up; live server acceptance and the deployed replacement cap were not independently exercised.

updates.ratingReason: Concrete participation improvement affecting queued miners, without treating ordinary competition tooling as a breakthrough.

updates.headline: SN127 Zils changes admission for commitments made before a pool opens
updates.summary: November 5 PR206 merged a rule that ignores model-body commitments made before a pool’s configured opening block, even after that pool opens. Earlier documentation had said those bodies would be admitted at the first round. Miners must commit after the relevant opening boundary under the new code. Flash and z3 opening blocks remain unset in the checked-in launch configuration; this does not verify a live opening or a deployed validator update.

sources.label: SN127 Zils closed-pool commitment rule, November 5

updates.headline: SN127 Zils operator arrangement disclosed; Astrid reports a 400 TAO OTC sale
updates.summary: November 4 afternoon carry-forward, already published in that edition: In its November 4 RNS announcement, Astrid Intelligence says Zils, founded by Ken Nicholson, will operate SN127 as an Astrid project. Astrid says it retains the subnet owner key and will recognize its revenues and costs. The issuer also reports selling 200,000 SN127 alpha over the counter at 0.002 TAO each, totaling 400 TAO, with the sold alpha unlocking on an agreed schedule. Its stated remaining position is approximately 3,000 TAO-equivalent, a dated issuer valuation rather than 3,000 liquid TAO. At 1:18 PM Eastern, SN127 Zils described its custom decision-model workflow: customers supply examples, miners compete, validators grade and customers receive an API. The November 3 rename and early-access site were covered in the prior edition. This follow-up adds the disclosed operator relationship and financing; it does not independently trace settlement, validate a lock schedule, prove customer traffic or establish who bought on the market before the announcement.

updates.headline: SN127 Zils merges disk-space safeguards for model-pool intake
updates.summary: Zils merged PR207 on November 5 at 20:12 UTC. The change reduces retention of graded model bodies after they leave the pool from three rounds to one, retaining hashes and sketches, and adds a 60 GiB free-disk floor plus room for the largest model body. Intake below the threshold is deferred to a later round without a failure or backoff penalty; ungraded models awaiting retry retain their weights. This changes validator storage management and miner admission behavior in code. Deployment across validators was not verified.

sources.label: SN127 Zils merged disk-floor and pruning change
SN127 Zils storage safeguards implementation

updates.ratingReason: A bounded operational change affecting disk pressure and deferred model intake, without verified deployment or adoption.
